test_title: PYST 69: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the following statements about Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme:

(1) The NBS scheme provides fixed per-kg subsidy rates for N, P, K, and S in non-urea fertilizers.

(2) Freight assistance is also provided.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme** was introduced by the Government of India in **April 2010** to regulate subsidies for fertilizers other than urea. It promotes balanced fertilizer usage across the country.
 
• **Statement 1:** The NBS scheme provides fixed per-kg subsidy rates for nutrients such as **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and sulfur (S)**. These subsidies are announced by the government annually based on the international and domestic prices of fertilizers. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2:** Freight assistance is also provided under the scheme to ensure the availability of fertilizers across the country, especially in remote regions. This ensures equitable distribution and accessibility for farmers. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Under the NBS scheme, fertilizer companies are compensated to sell fertilizers to farmers at subsidized rates, ensuring affordability for farmers while promoting agricultural productivity.
 
• The scheme applies to all **phosphatic and potassic fertilizers** such as DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate), MOP (Muriate of Potash), and complex fertilizers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purpose of the NBS Scheme:**

 
 
• To encourage the balanced use of fertilizers by subsidizing nutrients rather than specific fertilizers.
 
• To ensure an adequate supply of fertilizers to farmers at reasonable prices.
 
• To reduce the financial burden on farmers and promote sustainable agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Fertilizer Subsidy Structure:**
 
 
• The subsidy is calculated based on the nutrient content of fertilizers, such as the per-kg subsidy for **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and sulfur (S).**
 
• For example, if the per-kg subsidy on nitrogen is announced as Rs. 20, then a fertilizer with 10 kg of nitrogen content will receive a subsidy of Rs. 200 per bag.
 
 
 
• **Challenges with the NBS Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme focuses on non-urea fertilizers, whereas urea continues to be heavily subsidized, leading to an imbalance in fertilizer usage.
 
• Farmers often overuse urea due to its lower cost, resulting in soil degradation and declining nutrient efficiency.
 
• The government incurs a significant financial burden annually due to the fertilizer subsidy.
 
 
 
• **Steps Taken to Improve the Scheme:**
 
 
• Promoting the use of organic fertilizers and bio-fertilizers to reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers.
 
• Encouraging farmers to adopt integrated nutrient management (INM) practices to improve soil health and productivity.
 
• Digitizing the subsidy disbursement process to ensure transparency and reduce leakages.
 
 
 
• **Important Data:**
 
 
• India is the second-largest consumer of fertilizers in the world, with a significant portion of the subsidy budget allocated to the fertilizer sector.
 
• The government allocated approximately **Rs. 1.75 lakh crore** for fertilizer subsidies in the **Union Budget 2023-24**.
 
• Urea accounts for the majority of fertilizer consumption in India, followed by DAP and MOP.
